reverse.title: Trade-in refurbishment / reverse logistics
reverse.subtitle: Device receipt, cleaning, grading, testing, repair, storage, packaging, and dispatch.

stages.name: Smart receive
stages.confirmed: Trade-in devices enter through smart receiving automation. Brands include Apple, Google, Samsung, Motorola, and OnePlus.
interfaceQuestions: How is the device identity associated with its carrier, tray, or tote?
What transaction commits a successful receipt and releases the device?
openQuestions: Which conditions count as a smart-receive failure?
What is the physical and system re-entry point after hospital receiving?

stages.name: Hospital receiving
stages.confirmed: Hospital receiving handles cases where smart receive automation does not work.
interfaceQuestions: Who owns the exception and updates the receipt status?
What acknowledgment permits a recovered device to rejoin the normal flow?
openQuestions: Which tasks are manual and which are assisted?
Can exceptions be processed offline, or do they hold upstream equipment?

stages.name: ACS / AGS
stages.confirmed: Six ACS and six AGS systems are reported, with cleaning / grading chambers, pick-and-place robots and an integrated conveyor room.
interfaceQuestions: How do the chamber, robot, and conveyor exchange ready / busy / completed states?
Where are the cleaning result and cosmetic grade attached to the device record?
openQuestions: Are ACS and AGS separate stages, parallel routes, or combined equipment?
Which brands and models are eligible, and what causes a bypass?

stages.name: Manual cleaning & cosmetic grading
stages.confirmed: Manual cleaning and cosmetic grading are part of the reverse-logistics operation.
interfaceQuestions: How is a manually assigned grade reconciled with an automated grade?
What releases the unit to functionality testing?
openQuestions: Is this mandatory for every unit, a fallback, or a sampling process?
Which grade categories determine downstream handling?

stages.name: RATA / RADI functionality testing
stages.confirmed: Fifteen RATA and ten RADI units are reported. The site has fourteen Yaskawa cobots; their assignment across equipment remains unspecified.
interfaceQuestions: What sequence coordinates conveyor positioning, cobot pick/place, and test start / completion?
What prevents a device or result from being associated with the wrong carrier?
openQuestions: How are the 15 RATA and 10 RADI units assigned to products, and how do the 14 Yaskawa arms serve the equipment?
Which failures cause retest, manual test, or repair?

stages.name: Manual functionality testing
stages.confirmed: Manual functionality testing is another process in the refurbishment flow.
interfaceQuestions: How does the manual test result update the same unit history?
What is the release rule when manual and automated results disagree?
openQuestions: Which units require this step and which may bypass it?
Is it confirmation, fallback, or a separate coverage set?

stages.name: Radio-frequency testing
stages.confirmed: RF testing uses automated Rohde & Schwarz and Keysight systems.
interfaceQuestions: How are device model, software state, and test recipe matched?
How are measurement results and limit versions retained?
openQuestions: Which equipment models and RF configurations are used at this site?
Which tests run on all units and which depend on NPI or fault routing?

stages.name: Extended testing under RF
stages.confirmed: Extended testing covers device subsystems under RF conditions, including the terms PUCD / CDWRF supplied by the user.
interfaceQuestions: What conditions and results are linked across RF and subsystem tests?
What record distinguishes a test failure from an invalid test execution?
openQuestions: What are the exact meanings and scopes of PUCD and CDWRF?
What triggers extended testing, and what is the required sequence?

stages.name: Automated display testing
stages.confirmed: Radiant Test systems perform automated display testing.
interfaceQuestions: How is the device positioned and its test pattern synchronized with measurement?
How are display results assigned to the correct unit?
openQuestions: Confirm the equipment manufacturer, model, and local station name.
Which display characteristics and pass / fail limits are used?

stages.name: Peak-temperature testing
stages.confirmed: Peak-temperature testing is part of the described extended-test environment.
interfaceQuestions: How are device state, test conditions, and the temperature record synchronized?
What stops or invalidates a test outside its required conditions?
openQuestions: What is the test method, dwell, equipment, and acceptance criterion?
Which products require this test?

stages.name: Head Acoustics audio testing
stages.confirmed: Head Acoustics systems support audio testing.
interfaceQuestions: How are acoustic results, fixture setup, and device configuration traceable?
How does an invalid setup differ from a device failure in routing?
openQuestions: Which equipment model and audio tests are in scope?
Is audio testing in series, parallel, or conditional?

stages.name: Repair workcells
stages.confirmed: Repair workcells are part of the refurbishment operation.
interfaceQuestions: What diagnostic history is available to the repair technician?
Which tests must be repeated before a repaired unit can be released?
openQuestions: What failures route to repair and what are the other dispositions?
What are the return points, maximum attempts, and final disposition rules?

stages.name: ASRS, Locus & general racking
stages.confirmed: ASRS, Locus and general racking are reported. The site AMR fleet is approximately 60; its allocation between operations and tasks is not supplied.
interfaceQuestions: How is inventory location reconciled with process and quality status?
What authorizes retrieval or movement to the next operation?
openQuestions: Where does each storage or movement system sit in the actual process?
Are these buffers, reserve storage, order-fulfillment systems, or multiple uses?

stages.name: Quality audit areas
stages.confirmed: Quality audit areas are part of the operation.
interfaceQuestions: What audit status prevents packaging or shipping until release?
How is an audit finding routed back to the responsible process?
openQuestions: Where are audits performed and is sampling or 100% inspection used?
What rework, retest, or hold rules follow an audit failure?

stages.name: Automated packaging
stages.confirmed: Automated packaging is used before outbound.
interfaceQuestions: How are unit identity, order, packaging recipe, and label matched?
What is the response to a pack or label exception?
openQuestions: Which packaging steps are automated, and what is the exception path?
Are accessory kitting, sealing, labeling, and verification separate stations?

stages.name: Outbound
stages.confirmed: The reverse-logistics operation includes outbound dispatch.
interfaceQuestions: Which inventory and order events record completion and shipment?
What blocks a device with an unresolved quality or repair status?
openQuestions: What are the cutoff, carrier, consolidation, and departure rules?
When is a device counted as shipped in the reported KPI?

confirmedConnections.condition: Smart receive automation does not work

reverse.routingNote: Process families follow the described order. Their arrangement is logical, not a physical layout or a mandatory route for every device. The smart-receive fallback is confirmed; test bypasses, repair returns, audit positions, and storage interfaces need routing evidence.

forward.title: Automated forward logistics
forward.subtitle: Automated receiving, ASRS and conveyor routing, storage, packing, and outbound; floor VAS is the identified manual area.

stages.name: Automated inbound receiving
stages.confirmed: The forward-logistics section automatically receives product.
interfaceQuestions: How are inbound receipt and storage requests handed to the automation controller?
How are product and carrier identities maintained through induction?
openQuestions: What handling unit enters the system: device, tote, carton, or another unit?
Where do unreadable or unmatched receipts go?

stages.name: ASRS & routed conveyors
stages.confirmed: KNAPP conveyor equipment and an integrated ASRS environment are reported. Equipment quantities, layout and routing interfaces are not yet supplied.
interfaceQuestions: What coordinates conveyor route allocation and ASRS storage / retrieval tasks?
What happens when a destination is unavailable or a task times out?
openQuestions: Which WMS / WCS / PLC systems own each decision?
Which buffers and transfer points are physically available?

stages.name: Storage & release
stages.confirmed: Storage spaces are part of the automated forward operation.
interfaceQuestions: How are inventory availability, location, and release priority represented?
What prevents a duplicate retrieval request?
openQuestions: What allocation, release, and sequencing rules apply?
Are there multiple storage types or handling-unit conversions?

stages.name: Floor VAS / exception handling
stages.confirmed: VAS is performed on the floor in a designated section; the user connects this manual area with situations where ASRS flow becomes problematic.
interfaceQuestions: What moves work out of automation and what reconciles it before re-entry?
How is completion acknowledged without duplicate stock or tasks?
openQuestions: Separate planned VAS orders from ASRS recovery: are both handled here?
Where are the diversion and re-entry points?

stages.name: Automated packing
stages.confirmed: Packing is automated in forward logistics.
interfaceQuestions: How do the retrieved product, order, pack recipe, and shipping label stay associated?
What downstream signal releases the completed pack?
openQuestions: Which pack equipment and verification steps are present?
What happens on a pack failure or when outbound is full?

stages.name: Outbound
stages.confirmed: Outbound completes the forward-logistics operation.
interfaceQuestions: What dispatch acknowledgment closes the order and inventory task?
How are incomplete orders and exceptions retained?
openQuestions: Confirm outbound routing, carrier sortation, loading, and automation boundaries.
Which departure cutoffs govern release priorities?

forward.routingNote: Floor VAS is shown as a separate process area, not a mandatory step in every order. Its planned-work rules, ASRS-exception diversion, and re-entry points require confirmation. Outbound automation boundaries also remain open.

insights: Device identity is the connecting thread
A test result, cosmetic grade, repair action, location, and shipment must refer to the same device. Map the actual identifiers and reconciliation points before animating the route.
Engineering hypothesis to validate
A faster cell may not improve the whole operation
Inspect input mix, queues, shared resources, downstream capacity, and repeated tests together. Local efficiency gains need a separate end-to-end throughput and lead-time check.
Analysis question
Rework changes the effective workload
Measure repeat visits and repair returns separately from new inbound units. Distinguish first-pass yield, retest yield, and final release yield.
Measurement design
Automated flow depends on exception recovery

For forward logistics, identify who owns a failed task, how inventory stays reconciled, and what safely permits re-entry. Floor VAS and recovery should not be treated as the same process without confirmation.
Open interface definition

fulfillment.title: Retail + eCommerce fulfillment
fulfillment.subtitle: A shared inbound and storage operation feeding two outbound channels.

stages.name: South-wall inbound
stages.confirmed: Stretch unloads floor-loaded cartons at south-wall inbound. The brief gives four robots; the supplied marked layout shows three active docks.
interfaceQuestions: What causes automatic unloading to stop and manual handling to begin?
How does downstream conveyor availability constrain unloading?
openQuestions: Supply eligible freight mix, cases/hour, intervention records, and manual fallback resources.

stages.name: Receive, dimension & palletize
stages.confirmed: Receipt checks, CubiScan for missing LWH, and pallet building precede reserve or eligible direct-active putaway.
interfaceQuestions: How are missing dimensions and mixed-SKU pallets represented in inventory?
What confirms that the destination location is eligible?
openQuestions: Supply receipt cycle times, dock count, receiving resources, and dimension coverage.

stages.name: Reserve & active storage
stages.confirmed: 43,300 reserve and 12,768 active pick locations are reported. Reserve and active storage have different functions and location structures.
interfaceQuestions: What reconciles physical stock, location assignment, and WMS availability?
What authorizes reserve-to-active movement?
openQuestions: Validate CAD scale, aisle distances, SKU-to-location mapping, and resource counts.

stages.name: Replenishment & release
stages.confirmed: Replenishment is in masterpack multiples. More than five trips triggers a pallet location; unslotted material blocks a wave.
interfaceQuestions: How are replenishment completion and wave readiness acknowledged?
How are top-40 Specialty and CBK location rules prioritized when they overlap?
openQuestions: Supply replenishment triggers, demand distributions, trip times, and rule precedence.

stages.name: Locus each picking
stages.confirmed: Twenty Locus AMRs support eCommerce each picking, with the pallet area beside the tower and a north–south bridge.
interfaceQuestions: How do pick completion, tote identity, and induction readiness connect?
What controls traffic and queueing at the bridge and induction points?
openQuestions: Supply pick cycle distributions, associate counts, and verified routes.

stages.name: Pick tower, VAS & parcel pack
stages.confirmed: The three-level pick tower has active pick locations on Levels 1 and 2 feeding the conveyor, and approximately ten pack stations beside the conveyor on Level 3. Inline weighing scales and automated print-and-apply feed the shared route to downlanes. VAS is in front of the tower; Locus is beside it.
interfaceQuestions: What controls induction, accumulation, pack release, and parcel diversion?
What is the exact VAS route and where does it join the main flow?
openQuestions: Validate exact pack positions/count, scale and print-and-apply quantities, elevations, vertical transfers, belt connectivity, speeds, recirculation and interlocks.

stages.name: Retail pick & lane staging
stages.confirmed: Retail case / pallet picking feeds staging. Nine lanes with fourteen pallet positions are reported; Lane 6 is a known congestion point.
interfaceQuestions: How are PO, ship-to, carrier, and lane assignment represented?
What happens when a staging position or lane is full?
openQuestions: Reconcile the older all-LTL brief with later mixed retail / parcel lane descriptions.
Supply final lane map, departure schedule, and sort rules.

stages.name: North-wall outbound
stages.confirmed: Outbound is on the north wall and serves parcel and retail channels.
interfaceQuestions: What establishes shipment completion across both channels?
How is a delayed load fed back into release and staging decisions?
openQuestions: Supply carrier pickup times, loading resources, and shipment event definitions.

stages.name: Inventory remediation area
stages.confirmed: Damaged, unknown, or mis-received product goes to IRA for count / consolidation and then back to reserve.
interfaceQuestions: What inventory state prevents unresolved product from wave allocation?
What reconciliation authorizes return to reserve?
openQuestions: Supply exception arrival mix, resolution resources, and processing time.

fulfillment.routingNote: South inbound and north outbound are confirmed. This chapter describes system relationships; the CAD animation remains in Simulation. Lane allocation, travel distances, conveyor connectivity, and operating inputs still require validation.

insights: Release readiness connects storage to throughput
The confirmed unslotted-SKU rule can block a wave. Investigate how slotting readiness and replenishment completion affect release, rather than measuring pick rate alone.
Rule grounded in the brief
Downstream congestion can propagate upstream
Use the verified conveyor and staging controls to test how pack or Lane 6 holds affect induction and picking. Current animation demonstrates behavior; it does not estimate site losses.
Scenario to calibrate
More locations do not establish a throughput gain
The capacity explorer calculates location counts. Demand coverage, travel, replenishment effort, and staffing still determine whether an expansion improves operation.
Model boundary
The intervention record should explain the stop
Separate freight, vacuum/vision, reach, connectivity, and downstream causes when building the Stretch fault history. Link interventions to door-cycle completion.
Field-study design
